site.name: Tianyi Huang
site.subtitle: PhD Student, National University of Singapore

intro: I am a first year PhD student in Computer Science at the National University of Singapore, fortunate to be advised by Bohan Wang. My work is in computer graphics, with a focus on 3D shape design and generation.
I like building systems that are both mathematically clean and actually useful. My recent interests span graphics, geometric modeling, and generative methods for controllable 3D content.

Before NUS, I completed my bachelor's degree in Computer Science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. I still have a soft spot for compilers, computer system, and audio programming, so side quests happen a lot.

education.details: Working on computer graphics, especially 3D shape design and generation.
Highest Distinction, Dean's List, James Scholar, GPA: 3.97/4.00.

projects.title: QSynth: High-performance Multi-layered Audio Synthesizer
projects.description: QSynth is a high-performance multi-layered audio synthesizer written in C, featuring real-time audio processing with advanced instrument design capabilities.
how_to_play: Wait a few seconds for the WebAssembly runtime to finish loading.
Use your keyboard and controls inside the app to trigger instruments and layers.
Use headphones if possible because dynamic range is pretty wide.
If audio does not start, click once inside the frame to activate browser audio context.

projects.title: Octave: Music Programming Language
projects.description: Designed a language for programmatic music composition with notation-like syntax, variables, and functions, compiled into MIDI files.
how_to_play: Write or paste an Octave program in the editor.
Click Compile to generate and validate output.
Open example programs from the built-in links if you want quick starts.
Keep your favorite snippets in local storage for iterative experiments.
